s1.title: Read the clinic site
s1.body: A script reads the clinic’s public pages and pulls out the text: services, doctor, address, phone, patient reviews.

s2.title: Build the knowledge
s2.body: The text is curated into a knowledge file. Anything the site does not publish — prices, opening hours — is written down as unknown.

s3.title: The assistant answers
s3.body: Every question goes to the model with that file and strict rules: answer only from the file, give no medical advice, never guess.

s4.title: Booking and email
s4.body: When the patient accepts, the request goes to n8n, which sends back a designed email with the appointment, the clinic and a map link.

honesty.title: Why the email says "demonstration"
honesty.body: The clinic and the doctor are real, and everything here came from the clinic’s site with {doctor}’s permission. But the person receiving the email agreed to nothing — and a message saying "your appointment is confirmed" could send someone to a real clinic for an appointment that does not exist. So the email shows exactly what a patient would get, and says what it is. That is also what makes it safe to show any clinic.
